title: Skewers
subtitle: A pin in reverse: the big piece must step aside.
goals: Skewer kings and queens with checks
Pin queens to kings and collect

steps.say: A skewer is a pin turned inside out: the MORE valuable piece stands in front and gets attacked first. It must move — exposing the piece behind it. King in front, queen behind, rook attacking: the cruelest geometry in chess.

steps.prompt: King and queen share the e-file. Skewer them!
hints: Attack the king along the line he shares with his queen — he MUST step off it.
Rook to e1: check, king moves, and then...

line.say: Check! The king is forced off the file...
...and the queen behind him falls. That's the skewer: the king was a shield that had to move.

steps.wrongSay: Attack along the shared line — the king steps aside and unwraps the prize.
steps.successSay: Check-skewers are forced sequences: your opponent gets no say at all.

steps.prompt: Bishops skewer along diagonals. King in front, rook behind — collect!
hints: Find the diagonal that passes through the king AND continues to the rook in the corner.
Bishop to f3: check along c6... and a8 lies on the very same line.

line.say: Check on the long diagonal — and look what's at the far end of it...
The rook never had a chance. Long diagonals are skewer highways.

steps.wrongSay: The king and the corner rook share one long diagonal — get your bishop onto it with check.
steps.successSay: Rooks love ranks and files; bishops own the diagonals. Skewers live on both.

steps.prompt: Queen in front, rook behind on the d-file. Skewer the queen — safely!
hints: Attack the queen along the file she shares with her rook. But make sure she can't just capture your attacker!
Either rook can go to d1 — the other one backs it up.

line.say: The queen is attacked and has no good square on the file...
She fled, so the rook behind her is yours — with check! Note: your second rook made d1 safe; Qxd1 would have lost her too.
Skewered! The queen is hit first and must abandon her rook...
The rook falls with check. The a1 rook guarded d1 the whole time, so the queen could never fight back.

steps.wrongSay: Get a rook onto the d-file — the queen must move and the d8 rook is caught behind her.
steps.successSay: Skewers against non-royal pieces need SAFE attackers — always check who covers your landing square.

steps.prompt: The queen stands on her king's diagonal. Pin her there — and win her!
hints: Queen and king share the b1–h7 diagonal. A piece attacking along it freezes her: leaving the line would expose the king.
Bishop to c2 — and note your knight quietly guards that square, so Qxc2 fails too.

line.say: The queen is pinned to her king — she can only shuffle along the diagonal or take on c2, where your knight waits!
Nowhere to hide on a closed line — bishop takes queen. A full queen for a bishop.

rejections.say: It attacks the queen — but from off the king's diagonal, so she simply steps away. Attack her along the line she CANNOT leave.

steps.wrongSay: Find the line the queen is forbidden to leave — then attack her on it.
steps.successSay: Skewer, pin — same geometry, same lesson: pieces lined up with their king are hostages.
